site.name: Bitty
site.description: Favorite games, original experiments and a desk clock on tiny M5Stick hardware. An evolving project by Ryan Grams.
site.story: I wanted to build a game device small enough for my kids to sneak into summer camp. We definitely got caught. The project kept growing anyway.
site.intro: I’ve been porting some of our favorite games to a tiny screen, then figuring out how much fun we can squeeze out of tilt, a few buttons and an itty-bitty controller.

budget.note: My target budget for the stick. Check current store prices. Controller and adapters are extra.

hero.alt: Two translucent orange M5Stick devices matching the supplied Plus SE reference, with illustrative Galaga and Flappy Bird screens.
hero.caption: Galaga + Flappy Bird
hero.label: Illustrative screen mockups
hero.note: Illustrative Galaga and Flappy Bird screens in Plus SE shells. Public starter art differs. SE hardware testing is pending.

installation.note: The loader is public. Firmware downloads and flashing are disabled while USB loading and recovery are verified.

steps.title: Open the loader
steps.text: Open the link on a computer in Chrome or Edge. The loader checks for Web Serial support.

steps.title: Connect your M5Stick
steps.text: Use a USB cable that carries data. Pick the exact device model and its serial port.

steps.title: Load, then play
steps.text: When the release is enabled, follow the loader’s install steps. Compatible game files can be added there too.

devices.name: Original M5StickC Plus
devices.description: The original orange stick I’ve tested. New browser installation still needs verification. M5Stack lists this model as end of life.

devices.name: StickC-Plus SE
devices.description: A planned member of the lineup. Its own Bitty target and physical checks are still needed.

devices.name: M5StickS3
devices.description: A separate S3 build compiles. Sound, controls, Bluetooth and timing still need checks on the device.

controller.name: IINE Gamebrick Mini (Grey)
controller.description: The controller I’ve tested pairs in H mode with its yellow indicator. Pairing, reconnecting, directions, rotation and running jumps have been checked on the original Plus. Other modes and controllers still need testing.
controller.headline: Itty bitty. IINE Mini.
controller.story: I wanted to play some of these with a physical controller, too. It still had to be itty bitty, so I went with the IINE Mini.

games.name: Flappy
games.description: Tap to flap. The public build uses project-made starter art. Clock mode and experimental linked play are in the source.

games.name: Galaga
games.description: Our tiny-screen adaptation uses project code and artwork. Physical play-testing is still pending.
games.controls: Tilt to move, button to fire

games.name: Arkanoid
games.description: A native brick-breaking adaptation with project-made artwork. Release testing is in progress.
games.controls: Tilt the paddle; M5 launches / fires

games.name: Bitty Jet
games.description: A jetpack runner with project-made art. No extra game files. Release review is still in progress.
games.controls: Hold M5 to climb; release to fall

games.name: Mario / NES
games.description: Compatible NTSC NES cartridges, including a Mario clock mode. Bring the supported file and the rights to use it.

games.name: Tetris
games.description: Supported cartridge adapters, with experimental two-device linking. Files must match the preparation guide.

games.name: Geometry Dash / Famidash
games.description: Uses a supported, prepared Famidash payload. The guide explains the required format and limitations.

affiliate.disclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

features.title: A clock you can play
features.text: In the source build, each game opens on an animated clock. Press M5 to play, tap left to switch. Leave it on USB power at your desk or monitor.
features.status: New clock homes await device testing

features.title: Tilt. Tap. Try again.
features.text: Tiny screens and a few buttons are the point. Tilt controls work on motion-sensor models. The Plus SE has no tilt sensor.

features.title: Itty bitty. IINE Mini.
features.text: I wanted a physical controller, too. It had to stay small, so I went with the IINE Gamebrick Mini. H mode is tested on the original Plus.

features.title: Bring a second stick
features.text: Linked Flappy and Tetris modes are experimental. More two-player and co-op games are planned. Full two-device playtests are still ahead.

features.title: Give it a little home
features.text: I’m working on printable controller mounts and a desk dock with room to route a cable. STL downloads will appear when they’re ready.

features.title: Make it your own
features.text: Fork a game, add a clock face or build something weird. The firmware, skills and game-making guides live together on GitHub.

upcoming.name: Tilt racer
upcoming.label: Original concept
upcoming.description: Tilt to steer. Tap to jump an obstacle. I want racing that feels good while the whole console is moving in your hand.

upcoming.name: One-button runner
upcoming.label: Original concept
upcoming.description: A character runs back and forth. You get one job: jump at the right moment. Small screen, very little room to blame the controls.

upcoming.name: Hockey Queen
upcoming.label: An original game by Ryan Grams
upcoming.description: Asymmetric air hockey: easy for one player, ridiculously hard for the other. I’m working on a Bitty version of my original game, with an iPhone App Store release planned too.
